In the deterministic interruption replay, retrying with the original predecessor, effect_key, and witness reproduces the same attempt identity, while changing only the witness produces a distinct competing claimant for the same effect identity.

In the control case, recomputing the tuple from a newer predecessor changes both effect and attempt identity even when the logical effect_key is unchanged; therefore that reconstruction cannot by itself suppress a duplicate logical effect after an unknown-result interruption.
No empirical stale-CAS or create-if-absent probe was attempted because the active two-write micro-slice budget reserved the post-witness write for this durable checkpoint.
inference: For the exact modeled scheme, the prior composite identity is replay-safe across an ambiguous interruption only if the pending original tuple is durably preserved and reused. The replay narrows the unresolved coordination requirement: durable pending-attempt state is needed before an externally visible effect if cross-invocation recovery must distinguish same-attempt retry from a new claim after predecessor advancement. This is deterministic role-local evidence, not proof of connector-level exactly-once, mutual exclusion, fairness, lease expiry, or real rate-limit behavior.
